solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Composure, a quality of one modelling flat cap?

definitions.meaning: calmness and good sense under pressure

definitions.text: a quality of one modelling flat cap?
definitions.meaning: someone wearing a flat cap for a photo shoot literally has a level top to their head

explanation.surface: A fashion note on the calm demeanour of a model showing off a flat cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word literally: a flat cap gives its model a head that is level. A flat cap is the cloth cap with a short brim, typical of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and sensible rather than flustered is the very sense of composure, a synonym.

clue.text: Came before Oriel College Oxford, ultimately getting university instruction to read more

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the three words of the college's name

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells the reader there is more on the back of the page

explanation.surface: A student's progress: Oriel, an Oxford college, then university study and reading instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters L, E, D of Oriel, College and Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that led up to something preceded it and paved the way, so the phrase means came before.

clue.text: Trace garment, maybe one that's returned

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment

indicators.note: returned says these two little pieces are turned around and read backwards

parts.note: maybe means for example, abbreviated EG
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Spotting the trace of a garment, perhaps one that was sent back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's returned' turns EG plus I into IGE, which follows VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a last remaining sign of something, which is what a trace is: a synonym.

clue.text: Elusive Caledonian head interrupting sermon, cloth getting annoyed

indicators.note: interrupting says the headland word breaks into the middle of the rearranged letters
getting annoyed means the letters are worked up into a new, agitated order

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A cleric's sermon is interrupted by the head of the church, and the man of the cloth gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting annoyed' rearranges SERMON CLOTH into LOCH MONSTER, and 'interrupting' puts NESS (a headland) inside it after LOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the old name for Scotland, and the famously never-caught creature of Scottish legend is elusive indeed.

clue.text: Dodges girl that's repeatedly wrong about love

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: about means the wrongdoings wrap around the zero

parts.note: more than one wrong is a set of sins
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl who keeps getting love wrong dodges the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places O inside SINS to make SIONS after EVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasions are ways of avoiding questions or duties, synonym of dodges as plural nouns.

clue.text: Gloomy pet fording river

indicators.note: fording means the river is crossed through the middle of the endearment

parts.note: deary is an affectionate term, like pet, for a loved one
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A sad-looking pet dog wading across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fording' puts R inside DEARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary describes something dull and depressing, a close synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Awful men, dead mean about English colourful character?

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and must be reordered
about says the mean's word wraps round the abbreviation for English

parts.note: a mean is an average, in the arithmetic sense

explanation.surface: A grim scene: awful men, dead and mean, around an English eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' turns MEN DEAD into DAMEEDN; 'about' puts E inside AVERAGE to give AEVERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry Humphries' flamboyant drag persona, with her lilac hair and gladioli, is a colourful comic character.

clue.text: See one entering total state of bliss

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

indicators.note: entering says the numeral goes into the word for total

parts.note: a sum is a total
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch someone enter a complete state of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction but is a cathedral seat, ELY; 'entering' puts I into SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Elysium is the paradise of the blessed dead, so by extension any perfect happiness.

clue.text: Forces doctor to heave leg

parts.note: a surge is a heaving swell, as of the sea
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: An instruction for an army medic to hoist up a wounded leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: In the armed forces a medical officer is styled a surgeon, so the title names a military doctor.

clue.text: Dry fruit served round community, thus consumed

indicators.note: served round means the fruit is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the palm

indicators.note: consumed says the community's abbreviation swallows the Latin word

parts.note: EC is the European Community
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written

explanation.surface: Dried fruit handed round a community, which then eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' puts SIC inside EC to make ESICC, and 'served round' wraps DATE around that.
explanation.definitionFit: To desiccate is to remove moisture from something, so it means to dry, as a verb.

clue.text: Head filmmaker once getting a mention

indicators.note: getting a mention means the producer's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Louis B. Mayer was the Hollywood mogul behind MGM, now dead

explanation.surface: A film director of the past being name-checked as the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic leader of a town or city is its head, so the title fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Old organiser of best odds for backing

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are run backwards, with a racing betting flavour

parts.note: number one, No. 1, is the best
SP, starting price, gives the odds on a horse

explanation.surface: An old bookmaker who arranged the best odds for punters backing horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for backing' turns NOI plus SP around to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Psion made the pocket electronic organisers popular in the 1980s and 90s, now an obsolete gadget.

clue.text: Perhaps one's chosen by current king about to stop plot

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to stop means the turned-round king plugs a gap inside the plot

parts.note: a site is a plot of land

indicators.note: about says the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A tale of the reigning king trying to halt a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes RAEL from LEAR, and 'to stop' puts it inside SITE, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are traditionally called the chosen people, so a member is an example of one chosen.

clue.text: Courteous and respectful worker given honour is first

indicators.note: first says the honour and the word is come before the worker

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour
a worker ant is the typical crossword worker

explanation.surface: A polite worker receives an honour, and that is the main thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing deference or homage, which is a respectful and courteous manner.

clue.text: Indicator contributing to Sino-Mongolian uprising

indicators.note: uprising, in a down clue, says the letters read from bottom to top
contributing to says the letters are a part lent by the longer word

explanation.surface: A sign of a joint Chinese and Mongolian revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NOMONG sits inside Sino-Mongolian, and 'uprising' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnomon is the pointer on a sundial whose shadow shows the hour, so it is an indicator.

clue.text: Sweet drink prices to change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters before it

explanation.surface: A sugary beverage whose cost is about to go up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of 'to change' but is fodder; 'change' rearranges PRICES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Persicot is a sweet cordial or liqueur flavoured with peach or apricot kernels, so a sweet drink.

clue.text: Body of troops pass gunmen regularly

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word for armed men

explanation.surface: A military unit marches through a mountain pass, with armed men at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of gunmen: U, M, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a long line of soldiers or vehicles moving in formation, a body of troops.

clue.text: In uprising, a state of confusion briefly occurs

indicators.note: In says the shortened muddle goes inside the uprising

parts.note: a coup is a sudden uprising to seize power

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word for disorder

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Political chaos briefly breaks out during a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims MESS to MES, and 'In' puts it inside COUP.
explanation.definitionFit: When something comes up it arises or happens, so the phrasal verb is a synonym of occurs.

clue.text: Spend extravagantly in French rendition of The Scream?

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to shout is to scream or yell

explanation.surface: A splurge on a French version of Munch's famous painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scream is Munch's painting, but here it is just a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out on something is an idiom for splashing money on it freely.

clue.text: Big bird flying, à la geese

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters taking off and coming down in another order

explanation.surface: A large bird in flight, behaving like geese.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed coastal raptor is a large bird of prey, with a wingspan over two metres.

clue.text: King's painful expression over famous brother

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
ouch is a cry of pain
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A king's cry of pain at the expense of his famous sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the moustached, cigar-wielding one of the comedy Marx Brothers.

clue.text: Flag announcement that drug is no longer available?

indicators.note: announcement means the phrase is spoken aloud, giving words that sound alike

parts.words: that drug is no longer available
parts.note: E's off: the E (ecstasy) supply has been taken off the market

explanation.surface: A notice put up to say a medicine has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the verb to tire; E is crossword slang for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or slacken, and to ease off is to reduce effort, synonyms.

clue.text: Time to accept mostly elegant non-European headwear

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, and to accept says it takes on the piece that follows

indicators.note: mostly removes the final letter of the stylish word

parts.note: urbane means suave and elegant

explanation.surface: It is time to embrace a not-quite-stylish hat from outside Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' only links the time to what follows; 'mostly' drops the last letter of URBANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cloth wound round the head is traditional wear in South Asia and the Middle East rather than Europe.

clue.text: Total common sense, to eat new bread and cheese, for example

parts.note: mass means the total amount, as in the mass of evidence

indicators.note: to eat says the good sense swallows the abbreviation

parts.note: nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Pure common sense: sit down to eat bread and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts N inside NOUS, making NOUNS; nous is British slang for practical wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically bread and cheese are uncountable nouns, taking no plural, so they are examples.

clue.text: Dostoyevsky partially raised in islands

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, says the extracted part reads upwards
partially means only a part of the novelist's name is used

explanation.surface: A fragment of Dostoyevsky brought up among islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The run STOYE sits in the middle of Dostoyevsky, and 'raised' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyots, also spelt aits, are small islands in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Explorer caught in southern extreme?

indicators.note: in says the letter for caught sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extreme
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An explorer trapped at the far south?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the setting: Captain Scott died on his return from the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated Terra Nova expedition to the South Pole, a famous polar explorer.

clue.text: Old poet who wrote of French and English prime minister

definitions.text: Old poet who wrote of French and English prime minister

parts.words: Old poet who wrote of French and English prime minister
parts.note: the poet's best-known work is spelt out: of in French is DE, and a recent English prime minister is CAMERON, together the title of the book

explanation.surface: A medieval writer seemingly composing about a French and British leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The work is pieced together from DE plus CAMERON, giving the Decameron, his collection of a hundred tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth-century Florentine writer and poet wrote the Decameron, so he is the old poet in question.

clue.text: Deep Throat flew north, travelling for noted work

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The Watergate informant Deep Throat flees north on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted work' means a work set to musical notes: Prokofiev's children's piece for narrator and orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's musical tale is a celebrated composition, a work written in musical notes.
